rows.note: Use this as the default choice for property that has been left unused or neglected and has fallen into disrepair.

example.english: This derelict factory was finally bought and redeveloped.
example.traditional: 呢間荒廢咗好多年嘅工廠終於有人買返嚟重建。
example.jyutping: nei1 gaan1 fong1 fai3 zo2 hou2 do1 nin4 ge3 gung1 cong2 zung1 jyu1 jau5 jan4 maai5 faan1 lai4 cung4 gin3

rows.note: Use this for a person, animal, or dependent abandoned by a guardian or owner.

example.english: That derelict dog now has a new owner looking after it.
example.traditional: 嗰隻被遺棄嘅狗而家有新主人照顧喇。
example.jyutping: go2 zek3 bei6 wai4 hei3 ge3 gau2 ji4 gaa1 jau5 san1 zyu2 jan4 ziu3 gu3 laa3

rows.note: This is the all-purpose colloquial choice for an abandoned item or piece of property.

example.english: This broken table has been left in the back alley for so long that it’s basically a derelict.
example.traditional: 呢張爛枱擺咗喺後巷咁耐，根本係無人理嘅嘢。
example.jyutping: ni1 zoeng1 laan6 ci4 baai2 zo2 hai2 hau6 hong2 gam3 noi6 gan1 bun2 hai6 mou4 jan4 lei5 ge3 je5

rows.note: Use this more formal term when referring to property that has been discarded or left behind, especially in notices or official contexts.

example.english: The notice says that derelict items left in the corridor will be removed.
example.traditional: 通告話，走廊上嘅棄置物品會被清走。
example.jyutping: tung1 gou3 waa6 zau2 long4 soeng6 ge3 hei3 zi3 mat6 ban2 wui5 bei6 cing1 zau2

rows.note: Use this specifically for abandoned or unused real estate rather than for an ordinary abandoned object.

example.english: That derelict property has been empty for years, and the district has long wanted to redevelop it.
example.traditional: 嗰座荒置物業空置咗幾年，區內一直想重建。
example.jyutping: go2 zo6 fong1 zi3 mat6 jip6 hung1 zi3 zo2 gei2 nin4 keoi1 noi6 jat1 zik6 soeng2 cung4 gin3
